title: Paid without competition by the City, and taken without competition by another public body
question: Which firms does the City pay under sole-source, emergency or other no-bid rules, that BART, the bridge district, the school district, City College or the housing authority also took without competition?
finding: 3 firms paid $100,000 or more by the City since fiscal 2019 under a no-competition rule also appear in another body's papers as a sole-source, single-source or no-bid purchase: 3 firm-and-body pairs, $211,944 as read at the other bodies and $11.6 million at the City. The overlap is small and ordinary: Seneca Family of Agencies (City College (purchase-order report), $184,033; City $10.2 million); Wested (City College (purchase-order report), $27,911; City $560,843); Oclc Inc. (City College (purchase-order report), $0; City $802,508). None of the large sole-source purchases at BART or the bridge district is from a firm the City also pays without competition. 6,194 City College order lines were read for this.
how: City side: payments since fiscal 2019 whose recorded purchasing authority is sole source, emergency, a waiver ordinance or another no-bid rule (the buckets of the “award method” analysis). Other side: board items of BART, the bridge district, the school district, City College, the housing authority and the redevelopment successor whose text says sole source, single source, no bid or without competitive bidding, and City College monthly purchase-order lines whose note says sole source or no bid. The two sides are joined on the exact normalised supplier name; amounts at the other bodies are authorisations or order amounts as printed.
limits: Name match only; no address or tax number is printed in the other bodies' papers, so for a common name the records do not show whether it is the same organisation. A maker's own parts, software licences and proprietary transit systems have one seller, and each body's rules permit a sole-source purchase with a written justification. A vendor phrase parsed from an item title can be wrong. The amounts are ceilings, not payments.
